plan.title: bug(release): release:e2e is denied at the Step 10 closed-verb gate, so the rehearsal never reaches the npm phase

narratives.Description: Rehearsal dies at Step 10 closed-verb-deny-missing for sentinel 0.0.1, so npm dry-run never runs. The recut allow must not honour DEFT_RELEASE_E2E inside evaluateClosedVerb, and production on deftai/directive with a real version must still deny even when that env is set.
narratives.Overview:
## Recut (set-level arc on this thread)

Bound by successor lean 5504166310, verified-claims table 5504171849, completed-arc record 5504178463. Charter open critique, spend N=1. The filed options (a) `--skip-tag` and (b) honour `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E` inside closed-verb evaluation do **not** bind.

## What happened

During the v0.109.0 and v0.110.0 cuts, `task release:e2e` failed at Step 10 `closed-verb-deny-missing` for `target=0.0.1`. The rehearsal never reached npm dry-run. `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH=1` was used as a workaround and is not a fix (#3156).

## Recut design

Rehearsal may complete without a human-origin grant and without `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH`. That allow must **not** be `evaluateClosedVerb` honouring `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E`.

Constraints (from the accepted critic findings):

- Do not teach `evaluateClosedVerb` / `evaluateReleasePublishGate` to honour `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E`.
- A rehearsal allow, if any, must still deny when the repo is `deftai/directive` or the version is not the sentinel (`REHEARSAL_VERSION` / `REPO_SLUG_PREFIX`), including when `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E=1`.
- `--skip-tag` on the rehearsal argv is not a complete fix: `skipTag` skips commit/tag/push, then `runRehearsal` dies at verify-tag, so the npm phase still never runs.
- Inventory first: `skipTag` / `dryRun` already short-circuit the gate without touching the evaluator; the rehearsal owns `REPO_SLUG_PREFIX` and `REHEARSAL_VERSION`.
- Optional (dominated #3916 AC3): if the env bypass remains, `OK (closed-verb-env-bypass)` must not share the authorized-grant shape.

## Acceptance

1. `task release:e2e` completes green against a throwaway repo with no human-origin grant and without `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH`.
2. Production `task release` on `deftai/directive` with no grant still fails closed at Step 10. Pin: production repo + real version + `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E=1` still denies.
3. The rehearsal reaches and exercises the npm phase (tag coverage remains; do not skip-tag as the fix).
4. Whatever exempts the rehearsal is keyed to something the rehearsal owns (temp-repo slug prefix and/or sentinel version), not to a forgeable env the production CLI on this repo can inherit.
5. CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

Does not close #3916 (dominated) or #4079 (skill recut, separate).

Refs #3527, #1910, #1095, #3156, #4079. Arc: successor lean 5504166310.

## Set-level critique: do #4000, #3916, and #4079 actually close the release-authz stall?

Anchoring a portfolio critique here because this is the engine-side root of the v0.108-v0.110 cut stall. The question is not whether each of the three is individually reasonable. It is whether **the set** closes the failure class, leaves a hole, or makes things worse.

mechanism-shaped: true

refutation-target: **#4000, #3916, and #4079, built as filed, close the v0.108-v0.110 release-authz stall without overlapping or weakening the production closed-verb gate.**

why: default motion; the bodies already claim a complementary split (rehearsal carve-out / human-origin grant / skill remainder). High-blast permission for N>=3 is unused. Operator asked for the arc yolo, then through-merge of whatever survives.

design-critique: warranted, because the lean changes closed-verb evaluation, grant provenance, and the skill that sequences an irrevocable npm publish.

## The failure class, stated once

An agent-run framework release cannot complete the rehearsal, and cannot record a human-origin grant for the real cut, so the operator is forced onto `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH=1`. That bypass is the same audit string whether a human just authorized npm or nobody did. The skill then asks for mint at the wrong time, names a Task verb that does not exist, and treats a rehearsal deny on sentinel `0.0.1` as a hard stop before Phase 4.

Observed: v0.108.0 shipped with `OK (closed-verb-env-bypass)` and no grant. v0.109.0 rehearsal died at Step 10 `closed-verb-deny-missing` for `target=0.0.1`. v0.110.0 repeated the rehearsal deny, used the env workaround the #4000 body refused as a fix, then minted `grant-20260902024531-e2f626` late via a live TTY after the agent printed `task authz:grant` (not a Taskfile target). Production Step 10 then logged `closed-verb-allow grant=...`.

## The three proposed remedies

| Issue | Layer | Claim |
|---|---|---|
| #4000 | rehearsal gate | `task release:e2e` reaches the npm phase with no grant and no `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH`; production Step 10 still fails closed |
| #3916 | grant provenance | a human-authorized agent publish is distinguishable, in a durable record, from an unauthorized env bypass; the agent cannot mint that authorization itself |
| #4079 | skill / cut shape | mint once at Phase 1 for the real version; name `deft authz:grant`; stop saying debug; do not mint `0.0.1`; document the two Windows restore env vars; `task check` not `ci:local` |

#4079 already asserts the split: it does not recut #4000 or #3916. This arc tests that assertion.

## Measured on SHA `3d8b42438d00bd8a504a79bc8f50d00fdf61ddb2` (v0.110.0 closeout)

- Rehearsal argv is `[version, "--repo", repo, "--skip-ci", "--skip-build", "--allow-vbrief-drift"]` at `packages/core/src/release-e2e/entrypoint.ts:299`. No `--skip-tag`.
- `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E=1` is set in `packages/core/src/release-e2e/entrypoint-worker.ts:19` and consumed only by `validateSkipCiIncident` (`packages/core/src/release/skip-ci-incident.ts`). `evaluateClosedVerb` / `evaluateReleasePublishGate` do not read it.
- `assertTagPushClosedVerb` returns OK without a grant when `config.skipTag` is true (`packages/core/src/release/closed-verb-gate.ts:40-42`). Dry-run also skips the grant. Live tag-push does not.
- Rehearsal npm dry-run is a later step of `runRehearsal` (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/rehearsal.ts:33-40`), after `task release`. If Step 10 dies, the npm phase never runs. Confirmed by the filed impact.
- Sentinel version is `REHEARSAL_VERSION = "0.0.1"` (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/constants.ts:10`). #4000 AC4 already refuses a carve-out keyed to a caller-supplied version string.
- Env bypass and grant are already different decision codes: `closed-verb-env-bypass` vs `closed-verb-allow` (`packages/core/src/authz/closed-verb.ts:254-261`, types at `packages/core/src/authz/types.ts:138`). v0.108.0 used the env path after verbal approval, so both authorized and unauthorized env runs share one code. v0.110.0 proved the grant code fires when a live TTY mint exists.
- Mint refuses non-interactive operator-cli stamps (`packages/cli/src/human-presence-mint.ts:215-224`).
- No `authz:*` Taskfile target (search of `Taskfile.yml`). `commands.md` already names `deft authz:grant`.
- Release skill Phase 3 (`content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md:225`) treats non-zero `release:e2e` as a hard refusal and asks whether to debug or `quit`. Phase 4 (`SKILL.md:235`) is where mint is required, immediately before `task release`. Phase 1 still leads with `task ci:local`.

Sister comments (in envelope as portfolio members, not as this thread's ceiling): #4000 `5503937901`, #3916 `5503938006`. #4079 has no comments.

## Audit markers for the critic

**`audit:skip-tag-collides` — option (a) on #4000 is not a local argv tweak.** Adding `--skip-tag` to the rehearsal argv would skip the closed-verb gate, but `runRehearsal` then runs `verify tag`. A skip-tag rehearsal that still claims tag coverage is a contradiction. If option (a) survives, say what happens to verify-tag and to the npm phase that currently sits behind a successful `task release`.

**`audit:incumbent-codes` — #3916 may be asking for a distinction the evaluator already has.** `closed-verb-env-bypass` and `closed-verb-allow` already diverge. The v0.108.0 log line is what you get when the agent path is the env bypass even after a human said yes. Press whether the real gap is (1) a new audit class, (2) a way to turn in-session approval into a grant without a TTY, or (3) making the env bypass look like a grant. (3) is how you destroy the distinction. #3801 (standing unattended mandate) is adjacent and out of this set.

**`audit:interaction` — do the three compose, or fight?** If #4000 keys a rehearsal allow to `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E`, does that become another env bypass that #3916 then has to classify? If #4079 moves mint to Phase 1 for the real version, does Phase 3 still need a grant at all once #4000 lands? Is there a path where the skill tells the operator the rehearsal is healthy while production Step 10 is now weaker? Does any one of the three make another redundant?

**`audit:worse` — #3156 is already named on #4000.** Turning the production gate green with `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH=1` is the pattern the body refused. A rehearsal carve-out that a caller can trip on a real cut is that pattern with extra steps. #4000 AC2 and AC4 are the claimed defenses; re-verify them rather than inherit.

**`audit:skill-only` — is #4079 mechanism-shaped, or a docs remainder?** Naming the CLI, replacing "debug", documenting two env vars, and swapping `ci:local` for `task check` do not change a gate. Mint-at-Phase-1 does change when a human-origin grant exists relative to rehearsal. Split those. If the skill remainder is dominated by #4000+#3916 landing, say so.

## Also worth pressing

- **Cost.** Three issues against one stall. Rank them if you would drop one. A single smaller change that captures most of the value beats a three-story merge train.
- **Ordering.** If the set is right, which must land first? A skill that tells the operator to mint at Phase 1 while rehearsal still dies on `0.0.1` still stalls the cut.
- **Parent claims.** Verify rather than inherit: rehearsal argv, `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E` consumers, skipTag short-circuit, decision codes, mint TTY refusal, missing Task target, skill Phase 3/4 wording. Line cites above are claims until you re-run them.
- **Injection / swarm lens.** This target changes authority and an irrevocable publish channel. Apply the lens. An N/A paragraph is theater.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-02T03:59:42Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Set-level open critique of #4000 / #3916 / #4079 at SHA 3d8b42438d00bd8a504a79bc8f50d00fdf61ddb2. Input ceiling 5504068351. Sister data in envelope: #4000 comment 5503937901, #3916 comment 5503938006. #4079 has no comments.

The write-back's recorded premise is that the three, built as filed, close the v0.108-v0.110 stall without overlapping or weakening the production closed-verb gate. They do not. One finding blocks bind. The rest recut the split.

### 1. Honouring DEFT_RELEASE_E2E in closed-verb evaluation weakens production — blocks-the-design

Evidence, re-verified at this SHA:

- Rehearsal argv is `[version, "--repo", repo, "--skip-ci", "--skip-build", "--allow-vbrief-drift"]` with no `--skip-tag` (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/entrypoint.ts:299`).
- `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E=1` is set in the worker (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/entrypoint-worker.ts:19`) and in `activateProcessState` (`entrypoint.ts:51-54`). The only consumer is `validateSkipCiIncident` (`packages/core/src/release/skip-ci-incident.ts:59-60`).
- `evaluateClosedVerb` / `evaluateReleasePublishGate` do not read it. Allow is the row env-bypass key first, then grants (`packages/core/src/authz/closed-verb.ts:254-261`; `packages/core/src/release-publish/pipeline.ts:32-40`). The release-publish bypass key is `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH` (`conventions/verb-classification.json:33`).
- `assertTagPushClosedVerb` already short-circuits on `skipTag` with no decision code (`packages/core/src/release/closed-verb-gate.ts:40-42`).
- Worker threads inherit the parent `process.env`. Production `task release` already reads `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH` from `process.env` when seams omit env (`packages/core/src/release/closed-verb-gate.test.ts`, "production path reads DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH from process.env").
- Closed-verb threat model is aligned-agent confusion, not credential forgery (`content/contracts/closed-verb-authz.md`). The release skill already records that a process-wide env leaks into nested tests and temp repos (`content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md`, Branch-Protection Policy Guard).
- #4000 AC4's example key is that same `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E` marker. AC2's "production deny / rehearsal allow" test can go green by treating "production" as "env unset."

Failure mode: an agent, or a fragment in CHANGELOG / issue text / a sibling envelope, sets `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E=1` and runs production `task release -- <real-version>` on `deftai/directive`. Step 10 allows with no grant. `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml` fires. The marker still reads as "rehearsal skip-ci," not as an authz bypass. A Phase 3 background worker in the same session is the leak path the skill already names for `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT`. This is the #3156 pattern: the closed-verb gate is red on rehearsal, so the proposed fix edits the gate with a forgeable env. Reviewer attention is not a control.

Disposition: do not bind #4000 option (b) as filed. Do not teach `evaluateClosedVerb` to honour `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E`. A rehearsal allow, if any, must still deny when the repo is `deftai/directive` or the version is not the sentinel, including when that env is set. Inventory before a new key: `REPO_SLUG_PREFIX` and `REHEARSAL_VERSION` (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/constants.ts:7-10`) already name what the rehearsal owns; `skipTag` / `dryRun` already short-circuit without touching the evaluator. Pin a regression: production repo + real version + `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E=1` still denies.

### 2. Grants cannot reach rehearsal, so #4079 AC1 and #3916 cannot close the stall — sharpens-framing

Evidence: `.deft/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:56`). `cloneRepoToTemp` is `git clone` (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/git-ops.ts:43-46`). The worker evaluates grants from `cloneDir`. Release-publish templates bind exact target surfaces; `wildcard_allowed` is false (`conventions/verb-classification.json:27`; `packages/core/src/authz/closed-verb.ts:133-151`). Sentinel is `0.0.1` (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/constants.ts:10`). Observed on the v0.110.0 cut: "A grant for 0.110.0 would not have passed that run" (#4000 comment 5503937901). Tag-push does not spend grants (`closed-verb-gate.ts:36-37`); rehearsal never calls `release:publish`. Spend is not the bug. Store + target + clone are.

Failure mode: #4079 AC1 waits for a live grant on the cut version before Phase 3. That grant cannot satisfy Step 10 on `target=0.0.1` in a clone with no `.deft/authz`. The operator waits, then still hits `closed-verb-deny-missing`, then still uses `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH=1`. Default expiry for `release-publish` is `1h` (`verb-classification.json:29`). A Phase-1 mint can expire during long Phase 3 (e2e + npm install/build) before production Step 10. The complementary split as filed adds a wait that does not unblock rehearsal and can burn the grant that production needs.

Disposition: recut #4079 AC1. Print `deft authz:grant -- --template release-publish --target <version> --confirm` at Phase 1; do not make a live grant a Phase 3 precondition; mint immediately before Phase 4 (current skill line). Phase 3 unblocks only via a recut #4000. Naming the real CLI, replacing "debug", dropping `ci:local`, and documenting the two Windows restore env vars can land independently; they are not mechanism-shaped.

### 3. #3916 asks for a distinction the evaluator already has; a new pre-auth channel is the injection hole — sharpens-framing

Evidence: `closed-verb-env-bypass` and `closed-verb-allow` already diverge (`packages/core/src/authz/types.ts:136-138`; emit at `closed-verb-gate.ts:65-68`). v0.108.0 logged the env code after verbal yes; v0.110.0 logged `closed-verb-allow grant=grant-20260902024531-e2f626` after a live TTY mint (#3916 comment 5503938006). Mint already refuses agent shells and non-TTY (`packages/cli/src/human-presence-mint.ts:204-226`). Dual-mint avoidance: `mintHumanOriginGrant` is the sole mint (`content/contracts/closed-verb-authz.md`). #3801 is correctly out of this set.

Failure mode: implementing AC2 as a non-TTY "human said yes in session" record lets the agent write the thing #3110 exists to keep unforgeable. Implementing AC3's inverse (make env look like a grant) collapses the two codes into one authorized-looking OK. Either path is confused-deputy / compositional-fragment: chat affirmation + env + a new audit class that reads as grant.

Disposition: do not bind #3916 as a third engine story. The pre-authorize path is the existing TTY mint, documented by the recut #4079. If env bypass remains, AC3 is a log-shape change (`OK (closed-verb-env-bypass)` must not share the authorized-grant shape) and can ride on #4000. Do not add a second mint engine. Do not treat in-session prose as `closed-verb-allow`.

### 4. Option (a) `--skip-tag` cannot satisfy #4000 AC1+AC3 — sharpens-framing

Evidence: `skipTag` skips the gate, then skips commit, tag, and atomic push (`packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts:521-565`). Rehearsal then `verifyTag` via `ls-remote` on the temp origin (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/git-ops.ts:96-114`). Empty stdout is `tag verify FAIL`. npm dry-run is a later `runRehearsal` step after `task release` and verify-tag (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/rehearsal.ts:31-40`). Phase 2 already uses `--dry-run --skip-tag --skip-release` for a different job.

Failure mode: adding `--skip-tag` to the rehearsal argv makes Step 10 green by not distributing, then dies at verify-tag, so the npm phase still never runs. Tag/push coverage, which the rehearsal exists to check, is also gone.

Disposition: drop option (a) as a complete fix. If skip-tag survives, say what happens to verify-tag and to the npm phase. It does not meet AC1+AC3 as filed.

### 5. Skill remainder that does not change a gate — footnote

Wrong `task authz:grant` (no `authz:*` in `Taskfile.yml`; `content/commands.md` already names `deft authz:grant`), Phase 3 "debug / quit" (`SKILL.md:225`), `task ci:local` still leading Phase 1 (`SKILL.md:174`), and the two Windows restore env vars. These are real cut friction (#4079 body; v0.110.0). They do not change closed-verb evaluation. The rendered skill is pack-generated (`SKILL.md` header); edits belong in the pack source.

### Injection / swarm

Triggered: this target changes authority, untrusted input, envelopes, concurrency, worktrees, and an irrevocable publish channel. Findings 1 and 3 are the lens. An N/A paragraph would be theater.

### Road not taken

I considered binding option (b) because skip-ci already uses `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E`, the worker restores the parent env, and a fixture can call "production" the unset case. That is the strongest reading of AC4's example. What would flip: a deny pin for production repo + real version + `DEFT_RELEASE_E2E=1`, plus a conjunction the production CLI on `deftai/directive` cannot satisfy (`REPO_SLUG_PREFIX` and sentinel version, not env alone). Even then I would keep the honouring out of `evaluateClosedVerb`, so a third env bypass does not appear in the same function that #3916 is trying to make auditable. Skip-ci is coverage on a throwaway. Closed-verb is npm.

### Rank

1. Recut #4000 (only engine change that can unblock rehearsal without the env workaround).
2. Recut #4079 AC1 and land the docs remainder.
3. Dominate #3916 except optional AC3 log-shape on #4000.

The set as filed is not three complementary slices. It is one gate recut, one skill recut, and one issue that restates incumbent codes.
